dedupe_keys.name: statistics canada disposal of waste by source tonnes of residential and non residential waste sent to disposal by province every two years since 2002

description: This table reports how many tonnes of waste are sent for disposal in each Canadian province and territory, split between households and businesses and institutions, and is the national benchmark for waste disposal. It is published by Statistics Canada as table 38-10-0032-01, formerly CANSIM 153-0041. Coverage is Canada, its regions and each province or territory every second year from 2002 to 2024, with the latest release in June 2026. Each row gives a reference year, a geography, a source of waste (residential, non-residential or all) and the tonnes disposed, for example about 10.2 million tonnes from residential and 14.7 million tonnes from non-residential sources in the latest Canada figures; companion tables give materials diverted from disposal by type and source. The whole table is available as a free download in CSV or SDMX form under the Statistics Canada Open Licence, with a DOI for citation. Caveats: the series is biennial and reported at provincial level only, some cells carry quality symbols or are suppressed, and the footnotes define what counts as residential and non-residential sources. Simulation uses: setting provincial waste flows to disposal in waste system and landfill capacity models, and testing diversion targets against the historical split between residential and non-residential waste. Related records: the Ontario landfill inventory (data-ontario-landfills) lists the sites receiving much of this waste, and the US EPA facts and figures (data-epa-sustainable-materials-management-facts-and-figures) give comparable US totals.
